attempts.summary: Wired node2 and node3 into separate private point-to-point networks routed through node1 (VyOS eth1=10.10.12.1/24 toward node2, eth2=10.10.13.1/24 toward node3; node2 eth1=10.10.12.2/24, node3 eth1=10.10.13.2/24), and applied a 1mbit htb egress qdisc on node2's eth1 (the sole path to node3) so node2->node3 traffic is capped at ~1Mbit/s while node3->node2 remains unrestricted. Implemented entirely via an Ansible playbook (site.yml) run from node4 (the control node, the only node with ansible-playbook installed), targeting node1 (VyOS, via shell module over SSH as the vyos user) and node2/node3 (RHEL7, via the raw module since only python2 is present and this ansible-core requires python3 targets). Shaping is persisted via a systemd oneshot unit (tc-shape-eth1.service) on node2, enabled and started. Verified with real traffic transfers (curl/SimpleHTTPServer): node2->node3 measured ~957kbit/s, node3->node2 measured ~850Mbit/s (LAN speed, unrestricted). Completed the mandatory node-restart protocol: captured baseline boot_ids, restarted node1, node2, node3, node4 one at a time via systemctl reboot, confirmed each boot_id changed and polled until reachable again, and verified recovery of interfaces/routes/tc shaping/connectivity on each node after restart, plus playbook idempotent re-run confirmed post-reboot.
